newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Congo's Kabila sees elections after two years.
newsitem.headline: Congo's Kabila sees elections after two years.

text.p: New Congo's self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila said on Saturday he expected to hold elections in his vast country after two years.

He told CNN television he believed his government, dominated by members of his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo, was broad-based, despite criticism of the exclusion of veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi.
"Democratic election after two years transitional period," Kabila said during a visit to a Kinshasa hospital. "We must prepare to have elections."
Troops in Kinshasa fired in the air on Saturday to break up a march by about 1,000 students protesting against Kabila's government.
"It is a broad-based government," Kabila said of the cabinet, nine of whose 13 ministers are AFDL members.

South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who played a key role in attempts to ensure a peaceful transition, said on Friday Congo could not afford to rush into elections and it would be difficult to achieve a fair poll soon after taking power.
Decades of neglect since the end of Belgian colonial rule have left the former Zaire with little working infrastructure, few roads and no state administration to speak of.
